# 2 Baruch Chapter 53 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** The Cloud and Waters Vision
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 53:2 — description of the cloud's waters

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "it-was-full-of-waters both-black-and-bright, and-many-colors were-in-it" |
| LOGOS | "it was full of waters both black and bright, and many colors were in it" |
| PNEUMA | "it was full of water — some of it black, some of it bright — and it had many colors" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** SOPHIA adopted LOGOS. The Syriac syntax presents 'black and bright' as a unified attribute of the waters; PNEUMA's dash-separated reformulation fragments the description unnecessarily.

---

## 53:9 — the final black waters

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "and-they-were-more-gloomy than-all-those-that-had-been-before-them" |
| LOGOS | "and they were more gloomy than all those that had been before them" |
| PNEUMA | "darker and more terrible than anything before" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** SOPHIA adopted LOGOS. 'Gloomy' (Syriac: 'amiqin) preserves the specific quality of darkness/depth; PNEUMA's 'terrible' introduces a connotation not in the source.

---

## 53:11 — the healing lightning

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "it-healed those-who-were-lying under-the-dark-waters, and-put-out-the-fire" |
| LOGOS | "it healed those who were lying under the dark waters, and put out the fire" |
| PNEUMA | "It healed those lying beneath the dark waters and quenched the fire" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** SOPHIA adopted LOGOS. 'Lying under' preserves the Syriac participle indicating ongoing prostration; PNEUMA's abbreviated form is acceptable but LOGOS is more precise.

---
